q: Do mobile phone and internet bills count in our carbon footprint?
title: Mobile and internet bills in Scope 3
short: Yes, as a purchased service in Scope 3 Category 1. Telecom invoices rarely show energy, so most companies use a spend-based estimate. Data centre and cloud services are separate lines. The phones and routers you buy are Category 2 if capitalised, or Category 1 if expensed.

ul: Mobile plans and leased lines: a service, Category 1, usually by spend.
Some operators publish emissions per subscriber or per terabyte; use that if your operator does and state it.
Cloud hosting and SaaS: separate Category 1 lines with their own methods.
Phones, laptops and routers capitalised as assets: Category 2.
Leased devices: see the leased assets rules.

p: Telecom is a small line for most companies. A spend-based estimate with the factor source and price year is enough; revisit only if your telecom spend is large.

senseible: Senseible reads purchase and service invoices; it uses quantities where the invoice shows them and otherwise gives a spend-based estimate, labelled as spend-based with wider uncertainty.
